questions.stem: According to Ohm's Law, what is the current through a 10 Ω resistor when a potential difference of 20 V is applied across it?
questions.explanation: Using Ohm's Law, I = V/R = 20/10 = 2 A. The current through the resistor is 2 amperes.

questions.stem: Which I-V graph represents an ohmic conductor?

options.text: A straight line through the origin

questions.explanation: An ohmic conductor has a constant resistance, so its I-V graph is a straight line through the origin. This shows that current is directly proportional to potential difference at constant temperature.
